checks.detail: How to Vet an Instagram Influencer Before You Pay: A 6-Step Checklist
closest existing title 0.50: How to Use Artificial Intelligence to Start a Business

It passes; this isn't a generic rewrite. It's built for someone about to pay a creator: a copyable request for specific screenshots, rules for reading the creator's own Insights data, a separate check for local businesses, comparing posts against each other instead of using totals, a red-flag table with "what to do" actions, payment milestones tied to disclosure and a delivered report, and a clear refusal to offer unsourced engagement-rate benchmarks. The FTC sections are suitably hedged: buyer/seller framing, "ask a lawyer", and enforcement framed as "usually". The method steps (median post, reach ÷ followers, engaged ÷ reach) are advice, not factual claims.

All of the value claimed for the piece is actually delivered. Weaknesses: the table conflation (country mismatch); possibly outdated API timeframes; a lot of reliance on API documentation to explain screens in the app (which the article acknowledges); and "Engaged-audience demographics missing → treat it as a sign of a small active audience" is more absolute than the article's own earlier caveat. Overall, about 30 claims (all Meta API facts and all FTC quotes) are unverified because only three of the seven cited sources could be read. Nothing read contradicts the article. Before publishing: (1) rewrite the "country mismatch" clause in the red-flag table; (2) re-check the Meta API timeframe list (v20+ deprecations) and every Meta quote against the live docs; (3) check all FTC quotes against the three live FTC pages, none of which were verified in this pass.

The Instagramaps homepage was read in full. Connecting your own Instagram to see engagement by country and city matches the allowed claim and is supported ("across countries and cities"). Comparing views, reach and engagement per post matches and is supported ("the signal behind each post"). Marketplace profiles, matching and collaboration requests match the allowed wording; one small detail is that on the free plans creators receive requests and businesses send limited requests. Free Creator and Business plans with paid plans from 9 USD per month matches and is supported (Creator Pro at $9/month). There are no product claims beyond the allowed list, and the ownership disclosure is present.
